article_title: Meta Reportedly Builds 'Meta Compute' Cloud Unit to Rent Out Excess AI GPUs, Rattling Neocloud Stocks
summary: Submission approvable with 3 minor warning(s) — file a corrections record on merge

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece using an Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis frame. 659 words, within the News 400-1200 range. Prose is neutral and clearly separates reported facts from what remains unconfirmed.
editor_notes.source_verification: Four sources cited. I decompressed and read every archived snapshot from disk and verified each against the manifest sha256 (all three archived hashes matched). source-1.html.gz (Ynetnews, ynetnews.com, 200): CONFIRMS the Bloomberg attribution, the Meta Compute initiative, the full leadership trio verbatim ('infrastructure chief Santosh Janardhan, Daniel Gross of Meta Superintelligence Labs and Meta President Dina Powell McCormick, Bloomberg reported'), the Bedrock-like hosted-models option, the Muse Spark models, and the Zuckerberg 'definitely on the table' quote 'in May'. It does NOT contain the stock percentages or the $145B capex. source-2.html.gz (Fierce Network, fierce-network.com, 200): CONFIRMS all Sid Nag / Tekonyx quotes verbatim -- 'Meta already has hyperscale economics, world-class networking, custom silicon investments and one of the largest GPU footprints on the planet', 'Rather than chasing mainstream enterprise workloads, Meta's most successful path could be selling bare metal compute capacity and AI infrastructure to sophisticated buyers', and 'likely large enough to support a fourth hyperscaler, but not a fourth full stack cloud.' (article renders 'Nag said' where Fierce says 'Nag continued' -- immaterial). source-3.html.gz (Sherwood News, sherwood.news, 200): CONFIRMS the July 1 date (7/1/26), the 'definitely on the table' quote 'in late May', and the sector selloff quote verbatim -- 'CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN, and Cipher Digital are getting slammed in the wake of this report'. It does NOT contain the 8.8/10.8/12.4 percentages or the $145B figure. source-0 (Cloud Computing News, cloudcomputing-news.net) bot-blocked with HTTP 403 and did NOT archive (manifest file: null). The three load-bearing specifics attributed solely to it -- Meta +8.8% / CoreWeave -10.8% / Nebius -12.4% (two of which are in the summary) and the $145B AI capex projection -- have no durable snapshot in the provenance chain. As a last resort I WebFetched the live cloudcomputing-news.net URL: it confirms all three stock moves, the '$145 billion on AI-related capital expenditure this year' figure, the leadership trio, the Zuckerberg quote (source says 'shareholder call in May'; article says 'shareholder meeting in May' -- equivalent), and Muse Spark unveiled in April. So the specifics are accurate, but their archived evidence relies on a bot-blocked outlet that did not snapshot.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No fabrications or hallucinated quotes found. Every direct quote (Zuckerberg, all three Nag quotes, the Sherwood 'getting slammed' line) appears verbatim in a cited source. All named specifics trace to a cited source. The only accuracy caveat is provenance durability, not truth: the two summary percentages and the $145B figure rest solely on the 403'd Cloud Computing News page, verified live via WebFetch but not durably archived.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. The automated 'loaded language' flag on 'definitely' is a false positive -- it appears only inside Zuckerberg's verbatim direct quote ('definitely on the table'), not in the reporter's own voice.
editor_notes.originality: Original. No prior Machine Herald article covers Meta Compute, the neocloud selloff, or Meta entering the cloud-rental market. Grep hits for 'neocloud/CoreWeave' were unrelated (d-Matrix inference chip, Upscale AI networking).
editor_notes.framing_check: The report is properly framed as reported and unconfirmed rather than confirmed fact: 'according to reporting by Bloomberg', 'reportedly', 'under discussion', a dedicated 'What We Don't Know' section ('The plans remain early and unconfirmed', 'Meta has not publicly announced Meta Compute as a product'). No orphan URLs -- all four body-linked URLs (cloudcomputing-news, ynetnews, fierce-network, sherwood) are present in article.sources.
concerns: The two headline/summary stock percentages (CoreWeave -10.8%, Nebius -12.4%) and the Meta +8.8% and $145B capex figures are attributed solely to Cloud Computing News, whose snapshot bot-blocked (HTTP 403) and therefore isn't durably archived. Verified accurate via a last-resort live WebFetch, but the provenance chain lacks an archived snapshot for these specifics.

All four sources are off the allowlist (editorial judgement warning, not a blocker); the Bloomberg-origin scoop is a secondary summary in each cited outlet, which is normal for a 'reportedly'-framed story.
recommendations: Where possible, prefer at least one reliably-archivable outlet for the precise stock percentages and capex figure so the load-bearing numbers survive in the provenance snapshot rather than relying on a bot-blocked page.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS. The article is substantively accurate, neutral, well-framed as reported/unconfirmed, and free of orphan URLs; every quote and specific was personally verified against a snapshot (or, for the 403'd source, against a last-resort live fetch). The single recoverable issue -- that the precise stock percentages and the $145B capex rest solely on a bot-blocked Cloud Computing News page with no durable archived snapshot -- can be honestly summarized in a public corrections note, so it publishes with a clarification trail rather than being rejected.
